title: One learner. One water project. A connected society.

perspectives.name: Citizen & Family
perspectives.role: Bring lived experience, ask questions and help decide what is useful and fair. You do not need to be a technical expert to take part.
perspectives.needs: Understandable information, affordable access, time to learn and a safe way to question decisions.
contributions: Your family notices where water is wasted and what makes digital learning difficult at home.
Your child records observations with a teacher and explains what the measurements do and do not show.
As a young adult, the learner can help a local business test ideas; a learning project is not a promise of a job.
You can ask the local institution who maintains the equipment and how to report a problem.
You can ask who used the data, who checked the decision and how to challenge it.
Your community can help decide whether the approach meets local needs and what should change before it spreads.
perspectives.action: Find an accessible learning starting point

perspectives.name: Education & Academia
perspectives.role: Turn the same local question into sound learning, assessment and supervised practice. Retain educator responsibility for learning and safeguarding.
perspectives.needs: Prepared teachers, inclusive access, suitable materials, safe data practices and time to review learner evidence.
contributions: Listen to families before designing activities; identify language, access and prior-knowledge barriers.
Choose a small water-related learning task and assess observations, uncertainty and collaboration, not just a polished output.
Connect practical learning to a suitable business problem without replacing independent assessment with commercial demands.
Develop local facilitators and agree who owns the learning resources, supervision and quality review.
Document assessment, data use and human review so that learners and families can question them.
Share reusable teaching practice across institutions while adapting language, local needs and assessment.
perspectives.action: Discuss educator and institutional learning needs

perspectives.name: Business & Economy
perspectives.role: Bring a real operating need, technical expertise and responsible opportunities to apply learning. Do not treat an educational prototype as a production-ready system.
perspectives.needs: Demonstrated skills, clear interfaces, reliable data, security, maintainability and agreed commercial responsibilities.
contributions: Listen to community needs rather than choosing a product before understanding the problem.
Help scope a safe practical problem and explain workplace constraints to educators.
Test whether sensors and data analysis can identify water losses, record limitations and have a responsible person review results.
Agree maintenance, operating ownership and knowledge transfer with the institution before relying on the solution.
Provide traceable evidence of technical decisions, security controls and escalation arrangements.
Contribute to local supply and skills capacity under agreed terms, without creating permanent dependency on one supplier.
perspectives.action: Scope a practical training and systems requirement

perspectives.name: Government & Policymakers
perspectives.role: Set public objectives, assign accountable owners and decide whether the evidence justifies support, revision or a stop. Government is an actor; National Capability is a shared outcome.
perspectives.needs: A baseline, a lawful mandate, named responsibilities, realistic resources, inclusive participation and independent review.
contributions: Identify who is excluded from learning or reliable water information and establish a way for them to be heard.
Decide whether teachers, facilities and safeguarding are ready before supporting a learning pilot.
Require evidence of practical usefulness and safety before moving from a classroom prototype to operational use.
Assign ownership, resources, procurement responsibilities and long-term maintenance before extending delivery.
Clarify authority, accountable owners, human oversight and an accessible route for complaints and correction.
Decide whether independently reviewed local results justify wider adaptation. Measure local ability to operate and teach, not only activity counts.
perspectives.action: Discuss readiness and a measurable institutional scope

society.decision: Which local need should the learning activity address, and whose voice is missing?
society.owner: Families and community representatives, supported by educators and the responsible institution.
society.prerequisites: Understand access, language, affordability and consent or safeguarding needs before collecting information.
society.down: Institutional support can make time, access and safe learning resources available to families.
society.up: Family experience reveals barriers and changes educational priorities.
society.depends: Academy needs these questions; institutions must address barriers rather than assume equal access.
society.evidence: Record participation barriers and community questions without claiming that learning has already improved water services.

academy.decision: Is the water activity suitable for this cohort, and what would count as demonstrated learning?
academy.owner: Educators and the accountable education institution; learners retain agency and can question results.
academy.prerequisites: Teacher readiness, safe materials, accessible learning support and agreed assessment criteria.
academy.down: Education strategy and institutional resources enable the teacher to guide a practical learning activity.
academy.up: Learners' observations and teachers' experience reveal gaps in the curriculum and support system.
academy.depends: Society supplies the question; institutions provide support; businesses can supply realistic constraints without controlling assessment.
academy.evidence: Review an observation log, explanations of uncertainty and a learner demonstration. These are suggested evidence, not recorded results.

economy.decision: Is the prototype useful and safe enough for the next supervised test?
economy.owner: A named operational owner and qualified reviewers in the participating business, with institutional agreement.
economy.prerequisites: Reliable measurements, suitable skills, secure interfaces and explicit separation between prototype and production.
economy.down: Institutional requirements and governance define safe operating and review conditions.
economy.up: Operating failures, user experience and maintenance needs reshape technical education.
economy.depends: Academy develops competence; institutions coordinate operation; governance sets accountable boundaries.
economy.evidence: Use a baseline, test record and documented limitations. No water savings, income or employment outcome is asserted.

institutions.decision: Can local people operate, maintain and teach this work without permanent external dependence?
institutions.owner: The institution's named service and education owners, working with trainers and operational partners.
institutions.prerequisites: Resources, roles, maintenance planning, accessible documentation and supervised trainer development.
institutions.down: Public objectives and governance shape the institution's remit, budget and responsibilities.
institutions.up: Front-line experience identifies rules, resources or training that need to change.
institutions.depends: Economy contributes operating expertise; Academy supports trainer development; Society tests relevance and accessibility.
institutions.evidence: Review handover, maintenance responsibilities and observed teaching. A signed agreement and actual assessment would still be needed.

governance.decision: Who can decide, who must review, and how can affected people obtain a correction?
governance.owner: Named public and institutional decision owners, with appropriate legal, security and independent review.
governance.prerequisites: A lawful mandate, defined data uses, human oversight, decision records and an accessible challenge process.
governance.down: Accountable rules guide institutional operations, educational practice and business decisions.
governance.up: Public concerns and operating evidence trigger review of rules and strategic objectives.
governance.depends: Governance needs evidence from all other levels; a dashboard cannot replace accountable people.
governance.evidence: Inspect decision records, review arrangements and a tested complaint route. This is an illustrative governance design, not a compliance certification.

capability.decision: What evidence would justify adapting this pathway elsewhere, and what must remain locally owned?
capability.owner: The responsible public institutions together with education, community and operating partners.
capability.prerequisites: Reviewed local evidence, sustainable resources, adaptable teaching capacity and accountable arrangements at each level.
capability.down: National objectives coordinate governance, institutions and education without assuming identical local conditions.
capability.up: Community and operating experience changes priorities; the next cycle begins with Society.
capability.depends: National Capability integrates Society, Academy, Economy, Institutions and Governance; it is not one course or a government department.
capability.evidence: Evaluate independent operation, local teaching and accountable adaptation against a baseline. Scaling is conditional, not an observed result in this example.

assumptions.label: Teacher capacity is available
assumptions.yes: Academy can support a supervised observation project. Institutions still need to provide time and accessible materials.
assumptions.no: Without teacher capacity, equipment alone does not create learning. Institutions must address preparation and workload before expecting classroom outcomes.

assumptions.label: Local maintenance has an owner
assumptions.yes: The institution can plan upkeep and knowledge transfer. Business and trainer support still need agreed scope and resources.
assumptions.no: An unowned maintenance task can leave sensors unusable. Business continuity, institutional delivery and public trust are then at risk.

assumptions.label: Human review and challenge are provided
assumptions.yes: People can review measurements and challenge decisions. Governance still needs clear authority and a lawful basis.
assumptions.no: Without review and a challenge route, an incorrect reading may guide an unchecked decision. Governance must resolve accountability before wider use.

rooms.name: Society
rooms.concept: A community learning home: a family table, digital safety station, neighbourhood questions and an AI learning desk.

rooms.name: Academy
rooms.concept: A library and practical learning studio: study desk, teaching circle, curriculum wall and a water-project research bench.

rooms.name: Economy
rooms.concept: An innovation and operations studio: prototype bench, systems map, cyber-resilience console and supervised professional practice.

rooms.name: Institutions
rooms.concept: An institutional coordination centre: readiness table, infrastructure map, delivery responsibilities and local trainer studio.

rooms.name: Governance
rooms.concept: An evidence and oversight room: decision record, authority map, review desk and public challenge channel.

rooms.name: Government / National Capability
rooms.concept: A national development observatory: connected regional maps and workspaces for education strategy, institutional readiness, economic development and SDG-linked evaluation.

academyZones.name: Student Learning
academyZones.meaning: Use the water question to practise observation, interpretation and independent judgement.
academyZones.why: A learner needs to explain why a result is credible, not only obtain an answer from a tool.
academyZones.outcome: A learner observation log with uncertainties and a short explanation of what was learned.
academyZones.next: Explore an appropriate learning starting point.

academyZones.name: Teacher Development
academyZones.meaning: Guide practical learning without surrendering teaching judgement to technology.
academyZones.why: A water-related exercise needs clear learning goals, inclusive participation and safe assessment.
academyZones.outcome: A reviewed lesson outline, learner feedback and an observed teaching activity.
academyZones.next: Discuss educator needs, readiness and a feasible scope.

academyZones.name: Curriculum Transformation
academyZones.meaning: Connect foundational learning, practical work and accountable technology use across a curriculum.
academyZones.why: One project should strengthen transferable capability rather than become an isolated technology demonstration.
academyZones.outcome: A proposed curriculum map connecting learning goals, assessment evidence and local needs.
academyZones.next: Agree learning goals and institutional responsibilities before planning delivery.

academyZones.name: Research & Capability
academyZones.meaning: Investigate whether a technical approach answers the local water question under realistic constraints.
academyZones.why: Sensors and AI outputs require verification, secure integration and human interpretation.
academyZones.outcome: A scoped prototype and test plan describing measurements, limitations and review responsibilities.
academyZones.next: Scope supervised practical work; external technical support requires separate agreement.
